$comment: The records the lobby gramophone plays: what each is, where it came from, under which licence, and what was done to it. Hand-authored except `outputs` and `measured`, which build-records.mjs writes after it encodes. records/THIRD_PARTY.md is generated from this file; edit this file and rebuild, never the table.

Licence rules (the founder's, binding): the composition must be public domain worldwide (composer died before 1955 and the work was first published before 1931); the recording must be CC0 or public domain on its own source page, or CC BY 4.0 with its attribution recorded. ShareAlike, NonCommercial, NoDerivatives, 'free to use' without a licence, YouTube, stock-music terms, unclear provenance, AI-generated music and Internet Archive 78s without a clear licence are rejected. music.test.ts holds every record to this.

Each recording was verified on its own Wikimedia Commons file page (the second of the three sources in order: Musopen, Commons, European Open Music Archive): `source.revision` is the page revision read on the retrieval date, `licence.statement` quotes the licence line on that page, and `original.sha1` is the SHA-1 Commons publishes for the file, which matches the downloaded bytes. Musopen's own site answered the retrieval with a bot challenge (HTTP 403), so its pages could not be read; the Commons page names Musopen as the origin.

transforms: the same chain for every record. Trim to startS..endS, mix to mono (0.5 L + 0.5 R), high-pass 60 Hz and low-pass 7 kHz (the gramophone's own band is 250 Hz to 5 kHz and is applied at runtime, so nothing outside it is worth bits), gain by `gainDb` (measured so the record reaches `loudnessTargetLufs` integrated), a 5 ms-attack peak limiter at -1 dBFS, a short fade in and a longer fade out. No dynamic-range compression. Then two encodes of the same signal.
Bytes: all shipped files together stay under 3,000,000 bytes (`budgetBytes`). A visitor downloads one format, about half of that, and only after the first sound unlock.

encoders.opus: libopus, 24 kb/s VBR, application audio, 60 ms frames, in WebM
encoders.aac: ffmpeg native AAC-LC, 32 kb/s, 24 kHz, in MP4 with the index first

records.title: Gymnopédie No. 1

composition.evidence: Published in the magazine La Musique des familles in summer 1888 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnop%C3%A9dies); composer's dates as given on the recording's Commons page.

licence.name: Public domain (performer's dedication)
licence.statement: {{PD-author|Robin Alciatore}}; Permission: "Public domain music from musopen.com ... The music on this site is given a public domain license, therefore, there are technically no restrictions on what you do with it."

records.attribution: Gymnopédie No. 1 by Erik Satie (1888), performed by Robin Alciatore, recording from Musopen (musopen.org), public domain.

records.title: Waltz in A minor, B. 150

composition.evidence: First published in 1860 by Jacques Maho, under Charlotte de Rothschild's name, and reattributed to Chopin in 1955 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waltz_in_A_minor,_Op._posth._(Chopin)); composed 1843 to 1848 per the recording's Commons page.

records.attribution: Waltz in A minor, B. 150 by Frédéric Chopin, performed by Aya Higuchi, recording from Musopen (musopen.org), CC0 1.0 Universal.

records.title: At the Fireside (Kinderszenen, Op. 15, No. 8)

composition.evidence: First edition Leipzig, Breitkopf und Härtel, plate 6016, 1838 (https://imslp.org/wiki/Kinderszenen,_Op.15_(Schumann,_Robert)); composer's dates as given on the recording's Commons page.

records.performer: Donald Betts, for Musopen (named in the file's own tags; the Commons page does not name the performer)
